correctness.rationale: The unambiguous-discrimination SDP reduces by label-transitivity to the minimum Gram eigenvalue. For \(k<N\), principal-submatrix interlacing gives the lower bound \((1-s)^k\) and a nonzero alternating tensor supported entirely on injective tuples attains it. For \(k=N\), an exact positive-semidefinite subset expansion gives the lower bound and the permutation sign vector attains it. The local protocol uses the exact one-system success probability \(1-s\); all conclusive outcomes suffice when \(k<N\), and zero or one inconclusive outcome suffices when \(k=N\). Quantifiers, positivity range, linear independence, and boundary case \(k=N\) were checked separately.

value.rationale: The result resolves an explicit recent conjecture for an infinite multipartite family and replaces case-by-case Gram-spectrum calculations with two short structural spectral witnesses. The exact full-length term exposes a genuine without-replacement effect: one local inconclusive result becomes inferable from the missing label. The theorem therefore supplies a reusable exact benchmark for correlated quantum-sequence discrimination rather than a routine parameter substitution.
